meta.title: Oopswhere
meta.description: Your USOS timetable, finally readable. Sign in once, through your university. No database, no passwords.

landing.title:
Which room?
You already know.
landing.lead: Your USOS timetable — clear, fast and always at hand. Sign in once, not every five minutes.

promise: You only type your password on ZUT's site.
Sign-in goes through your university's USOS. We never see your password.
We only remember your list of class groups — in an encrypted cookie, on your device.
Group timetables are public, so after that we fetch them without your account. Once a semester is enough.
wins: Two classes at once? Side by side, like on paper.

faq: Is this the university's official site?
No. Being official has its advantages. We leave those to the university.
We show the timetable and nothing else. Apparently that can be done.
What if USOS has a bad day?
We show the last timetable we have and mention it quietly. Everyone has bad days.
If you want to be. There's a button for that.
Nothing. If something's off, write on GitHub. We'll answer.

privacy.title: Privacy
body: Oopswhere has no database and never sees your password. You sign in on your university's own site (USOS), and we receive one-time access that we use only to read your list of class groups and your first name. We revoke that access right away.
The group list and first name are stored in an encrypted cookie in your browser. The server keeps nothing about you. Signing out deletes the cookie.
Class group timetables, lecturer names and rooms are public USOS data. We cache them briefly so we don't put load on the university's servers.
No analytics, no ads, no third-party fonts. The code is open — you can verify every sentence on this page.
